constraints: Metadata loading does not mean media is playing or that lesson completion was recorded.
A shared-link lesson player renders lesson metadata before playback begins.

feedback.reason: The player announces actual playback transitions without confusing loaded metadata or browser state with recorded completion.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Use a polite status for meaningful media state changes; keep focus on the active playback control.
details.scenarioApplication: When the player changes to playing or buffering, announce that state; leave the learner on the media control and do not infer server completion from loaded metadata.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Browser playback and server completion are separate; status should not claim one from the other.
details.errorCorrection: Announce a concise state such as “buffering” or “paused” only when the media event changes, and keep lesson completion tied to the service response.
details.transfer: A recorded completion event should be announced separately from browser playback when the service confirms it.

messages.text: A render can occur without a media state change, so it would repeat an unchanged announcement.
Metadata describes the loaded lesson, not that media has begun playing.
Reading the whole lesson on each event obscures the one playback state that changed.
“Player updated” does not tell the learner whether playback started, paused, or buffered.
Status can be announced without moving focus away from the playback control.
The lesson heading is unrelated to the player action and would interrupt media control.
Without a defined playback event, metadata rendering can trigger a false “playing” announcement.
Without a concise state name, the learner hears no useful distinction between pause, buffering, and play.
Without a focus policy, each update may interrupt the control the learner is using.

values.text: Announce only a meaningful media state such as playing or buffering.
Announce on every player render.
Treat metadata load as playback start.
Name the actual playback state without rereading lesson metadata.
Read all lesson metadata after each state change.
Announce “player updated” without the state.
Keep focus on the media control the learner is using.
Move focus to the status after every update.
Move focus to the lesson heading.

prompt: A shared-link lesson player renders lesson metadata before playback begins. Metadata loading does not mean media is playing or that lesson completion was recorded. Select an event, message, and focus policy for this case.

constraints: Users must hear which action succeeded without treating preview as proof of publication.
A curriculum author previews a lesson while a separate publish request completes.

feedback.reason: Preview and publication are separate outcomes; only the confirmed publish response should announce publication.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A status region communicates the resolved outcome without taking focus; suppressing duplicate updates keeps a single accepted publication event legible.
details.scenarioApplication: When the publishing service returns its accepted result, the author hears one publication confirmation and remains at the active editor control.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A status announcement need not move focus, but it should reflect one meaningful accepted outcome rather than repeated polling.
details.errorCorrection: Wait for the publishing service’s final response and announce that outcome once while preserving editor focus.
details.transfer: Separate local preview events from externally committed publication state.

messages.text: Repeatedly announcing an unchanged result on each poll creates noise; report the accepted publication outcome once.
The outcome is accurate, but moving focus to a nonmodal notice interrupts editing.
Preview and publication are distinct; preview must not be announced as a completed release.

options.text: Announce the confirmed publication result once; keep focus with the active editor control.
Keep focus in the editor, but announce the same publication status on every progress poll.
Announce the publish result once, then focus its notice while the author edits.
Announce preview completion separately and publish only after service confirmation.

prompt: A curriculum author previews a lesson while a separate publish request completes. Users must hear which action succeeded without treating preview as proof of publication. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The user must learn that the list changed without losing their reading position.
A notification center receives new messages while the user reads an earlier item.

feedback.reason: A brief count exposes the change while preserving the existing reading context.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A nonmodal status announces collection change without moving focus from the item being read.
details.scenarioApplication: A notification center receives new messages while the user reads an earlier item. The user must learn that the list changed without losing their reading position.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The count communicates that new messages exist; list navigation provides their individual details when the user is ready.
details.errorCorrection: Announce a concise number of arrivals and leave focus and reading position unchanged.
details.transfer: Use summarized announcements for background collection changes, reserving focus changes for explicit navigation.

messages.text: The message arrival should not replace the item the user is currently reading.
Repeating the whole list creates noise and obscures the new item.
A visible badge does not announce the background change to the current reader.

options.text: Move focus to each incoming message and announce the updated unread count.
Announce a concise message count and preserve the current reading position.
Keep focus, but reread every notification after a single new arrival.
Show the unread count in text, but do not announce it while focus stays elsewhere.

prompt: A notification center receives new messages while the user reads an earlier item. The user must learn that the list changed without losing their reading position. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The user must hear when a panel becomes available without being pulled away from the feed.
A streaming home renders the main feed before optional personalized panels finish loading.

feedback.reason: The feed remains the primary task; optional panel arrival should not repeatedly interrupt or delay it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A concise nonmodal status communicates a meaningful panel arrival while preserving the feed’s active focus.
details.scenarioApplication: A streaming home renders the main feed before optional personalized panels finish loading. The user must hear when a panel becomes available without being pulled away from the feed.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The primary feed should render independently; optional personalization should not delay it or steal focus when ready.
details.errorCorrection: Announce the panel’s meaningful availability once, without replaying the page or moving focus from the feed.
details.transfer: For progressive content, report consequential arrivals and keep the initial task stable.

messages.text: Optional content should not pull focus away from the primary feed task.
The title alone does not tell the user that the panel is ready to use.
Stable layout avoids shifting content, but users in the feed still need a meaningful arrival status.

options.text: Keep the feed visible, but move focus to each panel as it finishes loading.
Keep the feed available and announce only the panel title when it loads.
Keep feed focus and announce a panel once when it is ready to use.
Render the feed early and reserve panel space, but leave panel arrival silent.

prompt: A streaming home renders the main feed before optional personalized panels finish loading. The user must hear when a panel becomes available without being pulled away from the feed. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: Messages may arrive out of order; the viewer should hear only the accepted event version.
A shared calendar receives event changes with versioned updates and separate notifications.

feedback.reason: Version acceptance determines which event is current; the announcement names that accepted event change without disrupting calendar navigation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A status message can report the versioned event update; focus remains with the calendar navigation task.
details.scenarioApplication: The calendar announces the accepted version of the changed event with its new time while the viewer remains on the calendar control they were using.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The event service resolves version order; the status layer must not announce unaccepted payloads.
details.errorCorrection: Wait until version reconciliation chooses the accepted event, name that event and time, and announce the result once.
details.transfer: When several payloads collapse into one accepted version, announce the final event state rather than each arrival.

messages.text: Network arrival order can be reversed; an unaccepted payload might describe an event time that is no longer current.
A refresh cycle alone does not mean the calendar state changed.
“Calendar changed” does not identify which event or accepted time the user needs to verify.
Reading every event repeats unaffected content and makes the changed event difficult to locate.
A background event update should not pull focus away from calendar navigation.
Resetting to the heading discards the current event and date context.
Without version acceptance, an older arrival may be announced as the current calendar event.
Without event identity and changed time, “calendar changed” does not tell the viewer what to review.
Without focus stability, background updates can pull the viewer away from calendar navigation.

values.text: Announce a change only after the current event version is accepted.
Announce every event payload as it arrives.
Announce on every calendar refresh.
Name the event and its accepted changed time.
Say only “calendar changed.”
Read the whole calendar after an update.
Keep focus on the event or calendar control being read.
Move focus to every changed event.
Move focus to the calendar heading.

prompt: A shared calendar receives event changes with versioned updates and separate notifications. Messages may arrive out of order; the viewer should hear only the accepted event version. Select an event, message, and focus policy for this case.

constraints: The approver must hear the authoritative rejection and find a recovery action without mistaking it for success.
A finance service rejects an exceptional payout after the approver submits it.

feedback.reason: The accepted server result is a rejection; the status must identify that outcome and preserve a route to recover.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An announced status reports the server’s rejection, while the form retains the values and recovery action needed to continue.
details.scenarioApplication: A finance service rejects an exceptional payout after the approver submits it. The approver must hear the authoritative rejection and find a recovery action without mistaking it for success.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The client can show pending state, but it cannot announce success before the payout service decides.
details.errorCorrection: Preserve the submitted context, expose rejection as text, and keep the permitted retry or correction action reachable.
details.transfer: For consequential actions, announce the authoritative outcome and retain the minimum context needed for a safe retry.

messages.text: The payout form remains the repair task; the heading loses the submitted context.
The result is clear, but a recoverable service rejection should retain its permitted recovery action.
Activation means the request started; the rejection must replace the optimistic status accessibly.

options.text: Announce rejection and keep details, but move focus to the page heading after response.
Announce rejection and keep details, but disable retry until the page reloads.
Announce approval on activation, then silently replace it if the service rejects.
Announce rejection, retain payout details, and keep recovery reachable.

prompt: A finance service rejects an exceptional payout after the approver submits it. The approver must hear the authoritative rejection and find a recovery action without mistaking it for success. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: Only the response for the latest user intent may replace results or be announced.
A data explorer receives responses out of order while the user changes a query.

feedback.reason: The status must follow the response accepted for the latest query; announcing stale results misrepresents current intent.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A current-request identifier gates both result replacement and status announcement, preventing an older response from appearing current.
details.scenarioApplication: If query B is current, its response updates the result list and status; a later response for query A is ignored by both paths.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The same request identity check must guard both rendering and status announcements; otherwise stale results remain audible.
details.errorCorrection: Use the current query token before either replacing rows or announcing a response, and ignore superseded outcomes.
details.transfer: When requests race, bind result rendering and announcement to the same current request token.

messages.text: Discarding stale rows is insufficient if their late responses are still announced as though they reflected the latest query.
An empty result is meaningful, but successful current results also need a status.
Old rows are not current results while the newest query is pending.

options.text: Announce the resolved latest-query result and ignore superseded responses.
Discard stale rows, but announce every response as it resolves, including superseded queries.
Announce only when the latest query returns no matches.
Keep prior rows labeled current and announce loading on each render.

prompt: A data explorer receives responses out of order while the user changes a query. Only the response for the latest user intent may replace results or be announced. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: Users must hear meaningful result changes without hearing the entire list on every update.
A map search displays a large list of places while the map remains responsive.

feedback.reason: A short count communicates the list change; each place remains available through ordinary navigation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A brief status such as a result count conveys meaningful list change without moving focus.
details.scenarioApplication: A map search displays a large list of places while the map remains responsive. Users must hear meaningful result changes without hearing the entire list on every update.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The map remains a complementary view; each place is reachable through the ordinary result-list navigation.
details.errorCorrection: Announce a concise result-set update and keep focus in the user’s current control or list item.
details.transfer: Avoid replaying large collections when a short summary can signal change and the full content remains navigable.

messages.text: Replaying every place name overwhelms the update; a concise count leaves details navigable.
This reports selection, but not that the overall result set changed.
The list can update before the map; tying status to render delays the meaningful outcome.

options.text: Announce each place name as it arrives while the result list stays available.
Announce a concise result update and keep the list available for navigation.
Keep focus in the list and announce when the selected place details change.
Announce a new result count only after map markers finish rendering.

prompt: A map search displays a large list of places while the map remains responsive. Users must hear meaningful result changes without hearing the entire list on every update. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: A color or spacing change alone is not a new user state; meaningful widget status still needs its existing announcement path.
A design-system widget changes visual tokens while its keyboard interaction remains stable.

feedback.reason: Visual tokens do not create a user-facing state transition, but actual selection or error changes remain announced through the widget contract.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The widget’s status channel reports interaction state, while visual styling changes remain outside its event stream.
details.scenarioApplication: A token release does not trigger an announcement by itself; when selection or expansion changes, the widget announces that state while its current control retains focus.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The widget pattern owns state announcements; a token release should not create fake activity.
details.errorCorrection: Keep token changes quiet, announce actual selected, expanded, or error state, and preserve the control the user is operating.
details.transfer: If a token update changes focus visibility or contrast, verify those visual properties separately from widget status.

messages.text: A color or spacing token update is not itself a user state transition and would create release noise.
Suppressing all dynamic state also hides user-relevant selection or error changes.
A token name does not tell the user which control state changed.
A generic message leaves the actual selected, expanded, or error state unknown.
The theme panel is not the active widget task and should not receive focus for a visual token change.
Resetting focus on every widget state interrupts keyboard operation.
Without distinguishing token changes from widget state, a visual release creates spurious status events.
Without naming the actual selected, expanded, or error state, assistive technology users cannot understand the interaction result.
Without preserving the active control, token or state updates can break keyboard operation.

values.text: Announce a user-relevant state change, not a visual token update.
Announce each color or spacing token change.
Never announce a changed selected or expanded state.
Describe the changed selected, expanded, or error state.
Announce the new visual token name to widget users.
Say only “widget changed.”
Keep focus on the widget control being used.
Move focus to the theme panel after a token update.
Move focus to the widget root for every state.

prompt: A design-system widget changes visual tokens while its keyboard interaction remains stable. A color or spacing change alone is not a new user state; meaningful widget status still needs its existing announcement path. Select an event, message, and focus policy for this case.

constraints: The operator needs a meaningful change in impact or incident state, not an announcement for each telemetry sample.
An incident console correlates browser errors, release versions, and affected users.

feedback.reason: Triage status should reflect a meaningful incident transition rather than raw polling frequency.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A status reports a derived incident transition without moving focus from the operator’s current triage control.
details.scenarioApplication: An incident console correlates browser errors, release versions, and affected users. The operator needs a meaningful change in impact or incident state, not an announcement for each telemetry sample.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Polling cadence is internal; users need severity or impact changes, not each sample used to calculate them.
details.errorCorrection: Announce the new incident state once when impact or severity changes, and suppress unchanged poll results.
details.transfer: For monitoring interfaces, announce material state transitions rather than the frequency of data collection.

messages.text: The row update should not interrupt the operator’s current triage control.
Repeating unchanged state adds noise without conveying a new incident transition.
Raw samples are not user-relevant incident transitions.

options.text: Announce a severity change but move focus to its newest correlated error row.
Announce meaningful changes while keeping focus, but repeat the same update on every poll.
Announce meaningful incident changes while focus stays in triage controls.
Announce each telemetry sample as a separate incident update.

prompt: An incident console correlates browser errors, release versions, and affected users. The operator needs a meaningful change in impact or incident state, not an announcement for each telemetry sample. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: After rejection, state explicitly that no appointment was booked and keep Retry reachable.
Retain the chosen appointment slot so the patient can retry without selecting a time again.

feedback.reason: A failed confirmation cannot be announced or displayed as a booking; the user needs the actual outcome and recovery action.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A result announcement communicates booking state while retained form values preserve a direct recovery path.
details.scenarioApplication: After rejection, the patient hears that no booking exists; the chosen slot remains selected and the nearby Retry action can resubmit it.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Pending describes an unresolved request; after rejection, the result must clarify that no booking was confirmed.
details.errorCorrection: Keep the selected slot, announce that no appointment was booked, and offer retry without claiming success.
details.transfer: For a recoverable reservation failure, state that nothing was booked and preserve the user’s chosen option through retry.

messages.text: A pending label and generic retryable error leave the patient unsure whether a booking exists; state clearly that no appointment was made.
The result is clear, but retaining selection makes a recoverable retry possible without repeating work.
The home page interrupts the repair flow and separates the user from their selected appointment.

options.text: Keep the request pending and announce a retryable error without saying whether an appointment was booked.
Announce booking failure and retry, but require the patient to reselect the slot.
Keep the selected details and announce failure, but send focus to the clinic home page.
State no booking was made; retain the selected slot and offer retry.

prompt: A clinic booking request fails confirmation after the patient submits an appointment. The patient must hear that no booking was made, retain the selected slot for an immediate retry, and have a reachable recovery action. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The user must know which provider failed without losing valid options or hearing the whole result list repeated.
A travel search receives partial failures from providers while other results remain healthy.

feedback.reason: The failure is scoped to one provider; a concise message preserves healthy options and names the recoverable issue.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A concise status scopes partial failure to the affected provider and preserves unaffected result content and focus.
details.scenarioApplication: A travel search receives partial failures from providers while other results remain healthy. The user must know which provider failed without losing valid options or hearing the whole result list repeated.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A blocking error is appropriate only if no usable provider result remains.
details.errorCorrection: Name the failed provider in text, preserve healthy choices, and expose a retry where that provider supports recovery.
details.transfer: When a multi-source task partially succeeds, announce only the changed source and retain successful work.

messages.text: A nonmodal failure should not interrupt users who are reviewing valid options.
Repeating healthy results obscures the provider whose state actually changed.
The status identifies the fault but leaves no next step when retry is supported.

options.text: Name the failed provider and retry path while preserving healthy results and focus.
Keep healthy results and name the failed provider, but focus its Retry control.
Name the failed provider and keep valid options, but reread them on each retry.
Keep healthy results and name the failed provider, but omit any available recovery action.

prompt: A travel search receives partial failures from providers while other results remain healthy. The user must know which provider failed without losing valid options or hearing the whole result list repeated. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The call may remain active when only one subsystem fails; the user needs a scoped, truthful status.
A video call switches devices where signaling, media, permission, and relay can fail independently.

feedback.reason: A device-switch result should identify its failing subsystem without implying the entire call stopped or moving focus away from the switch control.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The call remains the active nonmodal task; its status identifies the resolved device subsystem without moving focus.
details.scenarioApplication: If microphone permission fails during device switching, announce that specific outcome, keep focus on the switch control, and leave the existing call state intact.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A service-level call failure may require a broader alert; isolated device failure does not.
details.errorCorrection: Report the named subsystem failure after it resolves; do not translate one device error into total call failure or success.
details.transfer: If the new device becomes active, announce its confirmed name after media reports the switch succeeded.

messages.text: A device permission error can leave the existing call working, so total call failure overstates the impact.
Signaling samples are implementation activity, not separate user outcomes.
The user cannot tell whether permission, media, or relay needs recovery from a generic error.
Starting a switch request does not establish that the new device is active.
A nonmodal status can be announced while the user remains on the device-switch control.
Opening settings during a call does not make background call controls part of a modal trap.
Without waiting for a resolved subsystem result, a request can be announced as a failure before it completes.
Without naming the affected subsystem, the user cannot choose the correct device recovery.
Without stable focus, a nonmodal device status interrupts the active call control.

values.text: Announce the specific subsystem result after it resolves.
Announce total call failure for any device error.
Announce every signaling and relay sample.
Name the device and whether permission, media, or relay failed.
Say only “device switch failed.”
Announce switch success when the request starts.
Keep focus on the device switch control while status appears.
Move focus to every subsystem update.
Trap focus in device settings during the call.

prompt: A video call switches devices where signaling, media, permission, and relay can fail independently. The call may remain active when only one subsystem fails; the user needs a scoped, truthful status. Select an event, message, and focus policy for this case.

constraints: A completed scan should be announced without requiring motion or moving focus away from the next item.
A warehouse handheld scanner supports keyboard, touch, camera, and reduced-motion use.

feedback.reason: Text status remains perceivable with reduced motion; stable focus supports repeated scans across input modes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A short text status reports scan completion independent of animation and without moving focus from the repeated workflow.
details.scenarioApplication: A warehouse handheld scanner supports keyboard, touch, camera, and reduced-motion use. A completed scan should be announced without requiring motion or moving focus away from the next item.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A camera preview can remain available on request, but the completion signal must work with keyboard and reduced motion.
details.errorCorrection: Announce the scanned item or result in text and leave focus at the next scan action.
details.transfer: For repeated input workflows, make each outcome perceivable without animation and keep the next action ready.

messages.text: Text must carry the confirmation so reduced-motion users do not depend on animation.
The next action is ready, but replaying the inventory overwhelms a one-item result.
Animation alone is not a text announcement and may be unavailable with reduced motion.

options.text: Announce text and keep scan flow, but use motion as the primary success cue.
Announce the scanned item in text and keep focus on the next scan action.
Read the full inventory after each scan and keep focus on the next item.
Use an animation as the scan result and leave the status channel silent.

prompt: A warehouse handheld scanner supports keyboard, touch, camera, and reduced-motion use. A completed scan should be announced without requiring motion or moving focus away from the next item. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The user must hear the accepted revocation once, while a stale tab must not announce the session as active.
A session is revoked in one security-settings tab while another tab remains open.

feedback.reason: The status must follow the accepted revocation state rather than a tab’s stale local snapshot.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Cross-tab state reconciliation prevents a second view from continuing to report a revoked session as active.
details.scenarioApplication: The initiating tab announces the accepted revocation once; another open tab updates its state before it tells the user whether that session remains active.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The announcement reports revocation but does not itself invalidate credentials or synchronize tabs.
details.errorCorrection: After server acceptance, distribute the revoked session state to open tabs and announce the confirmation only once.
details.transfer: For shared state across views, bind announcements to the canonical event and suppress duplicate or superseded snapshots.

messages.text: Confirmation in one tab does not correct a stale active state elsewhere; reconcile the other tab before presenting its session status.
Each tab can repeat the same event; the accepted change should be announced once.
Cross-tab deduplication does not remove the need for an announced confirmation.

options.text: Announce accepted revocation in the initiating tab, but leave another stale tab showing the session as active.
Announce the accepted revocation in every tab that observes the update.
Announce confirmed revocation once; reconcile stale tabs before status.
Reconcile the state but expose revocation only through a visual badge.

prompt: A session is revoked in one security-settings tab while another tab remains open. The user must hear the accepted revocation once, while a stale tab must not announce the session as active. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The inspector must hear that the draft is saved locally but not yet synchronized, without losing focus in the form.
An offline field inspection keeps a durable local draft while synchronization is unavailable.

feedback.reason: Local save and server synchronization are separate states; the status must not claim submission before connectivity returns.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Local persistence and remote receipt are different completion events, so each needs its own truthful status.
details.scenarioApplication: The device confirms that the local write is durable, then separately reports synchronization as pending until a later server acknowledgement.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A durable local write can be confirmed offline, but server submission requires a separate accepted response.
details.errorCorrection: Announce local save as local and keep synchronization pending until the server confirms receipt.
details.transfer: When offline work has multiple durability stages, name each stage rather than collapsing them into “saved” or “submitted.”

messages.text: Local durability does not mean the server received the draft; announce the saved-on-device state and pending sync separately.
Connectivity checks are background updates, not a reason to move focus repeatedly.
The text is helpful, but the user still cannot hear that the local draft survived.

options.text: Announce the durable local save as submitted to the server, without moving focus.
Announce pending sync and focus the offline banner on each connectivity check.
Show a text offline state, but announce local save only after reconnect.
Announce local save and pending sync separately; keep focus in the form.

prompt: An offline field inspection keeps a durable local draft while synchronization is unavailable. The inspector must hear that the draft is saved locally but not yet synchronized, without losing focus in the form. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: Presence can change often, but the reply remains the user’s saved work and must not be interrupted by each update.
A support inbox shows short-lived presence updates beside a durable reply draft.

feedback.reason: Ephemeral presence and durable reply state have different meanings; separate concise messages keep the reply task intact.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Presence and reply delivery use distinct status events because one is ephemeral and the other durable.
details.scenarioApplication: Meaningful participant arrivals can be summarized, the reply’s saved or sent state is announced independently, and presence changes do not move focus from the composer.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Presence is not a send confirmation; only the reply service reports durable delivery.
details.errorCorrection: Announce a concise presence transition when useful, and report saved or sent only from the reply service result.
details.transfer: If a reply fails to send, identify that failure while keeping the draft available; presence does not alter its delivery state.

messages.text: Heartbeat polling is not a meaningful participant transition and would flood the inbox status channel.
Suppressing all presence hides useful availability changes instead of summarizing them.
Presence only indicates availability and cannot prove the reply was saved or delivered.
Combining presence and reply status makes an ephemeral signal look like durable delivery.
A background availability change should not interrupt composing a reply.
Presence is unrelated to the user’s draft and clearing it discards work.
Without a meaningful presence policy, heartbeat changes either overwhelm the inbox or hide useful availability.
Without a separate durable reply result, agent presence can be mistaken for message delivery.
Without preserving composer focus, ephemeral presence interrupts the user’s unsent draft.

values.text: Announce only meaningful presence transitions or a concise participant count.
Announce every presence heartbeat.
Never expose another agent’s availability.
Announce the reply’s saved or sent result separately from presence.
Treat active presence as proof the reply was sent.
Use one generic status for presence and reply state.
Keep focus in the reply composer during background presence changes.
Move focus to every agent who becomes active.
Clear the draft when presence changes.

prompt: A support inbox shows short-lived presence updates beside a durable reply draft. Presence can change often, but the reply remains the user’s saved work and must not be interrupted by each update. Select an event, message, and focus policy for this case.

constraints: Loading personal controls must not be announced as if the public article or publication state changed.
A public article is crawler-visible while personalized controls use a separate cache boundary.

feedback.reason: The personalized control update is separate from article content and cache state; only its relevant outcome should be announced.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Separate status messages follow the state that changed; a personalized control refresh is not evidence of a public article update.
details.scenarioApplication: Personal-control hydration reports only that control state; the public article remains unchanged and no article-publication message is emitted.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Separate cache lifetimes do not imply a public-content publication event when personal controls load.
details.errorCorrection: Announce the changed personal control state only, and do not announce or vary the public article unless it actually changes.
details.transfer: When public and personalized content have separate lifetimes, report only the state that changed.

messages.text: A nonmodal control update should not take focus from the public article.
Hydrating a personal control does not republish the public article; that message reports a state change that did not occur.
The article did not change; replaying it conflates separate content states.

options.text: Announce only the personalized-control change, not the public article.
Announce the personal control state when it changes, but move focus there on hydration.
Announce that the public article was republished whenever personal controls hydrate.
Announce the full public article whenever personal controls hydrate.

prompt: A public article is crawler-visible while personalized controls use a separate cache boundary. Loading personal controls must not be announced as if the public article or publication state changed. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The fleet manager must hear when data becomes stale or refresh completes without an announcement for every poll.
A fleet dashboard refreshes at intervals over a slow network with a bounded freshness budget.

feedback.reason: The bounded freshness state matters to the user; routine unchanged polls do not.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A status announces meaningful freshness transitions while routine unchanged polls stay silent.
details.scenarioApplication: A fleet dashboard refreshes at intervals over a slow network with a bounded freshness budget. The fleet manager must hear when data becomes stale or refresh completes without an announcement for every poll.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The freshness budget determines when data is stale; poll cadence itself is not a user-facing state.
details.errorCorrection: Announce accepted refresh completion or stale transition once and retain the current focus location.
details.transfer: For periodic data, communicate freshness and meaningful changes rather than each timer tick.

messages.text: Successful refresh completion also tells the manager the current data is available.
Unchanged polls repeat implementation activity rather than a new freshness outcome.
A background refresh should not interrupt the manager’s current dashboard task.

options.text: Announce staleness only, and omit a successful refresh within the freshness budget.
Announce stale or refreshed state; suppress unchanged polls.

prompt: A fleet dashboard refreshes at intervals over a slow network with a bounded freshness budget. The fleet manager must hear when data becomes stale or refresh completes without an announcement for every poll. Which announcement and focus decision communicates the real outcome?

constraints: The producer must identify which subsystem changed and recover without a generic status implying all work failed.
An audio production studio has independent playback, marker, and upload failures.

feedback.reason: Independent subsystems need scoped status so one failure does not imply that unrelated work also failed.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Scoped status names the subsystem that changed while leaving focus and unrelated controls available.
details.scenarioApplication: An audio production studio has independent playback, marker, and upload failures. The producer must identify which subsystem changed and recover without a generic status implying all work failed.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A global blocking alert is justified only when a shared failure actually interrupts every studio task.
details.errorCorrection: Identify the failing subsystem, retain healthy work, and provide recovery next to the affected control without forced focus movement.
details.transfer: When independent subsystems fail separately, keep their state, messages, and recovery paths separate.

messages.text: The status can be announced without interrupting the active studio control.
The scope is clear, but the producer still needs a way to recover the affected subsystem.
A generic message hides which independent subsystem failed and which work remains available.
